items.title: Did Zero Copy Data Sharing Just Shift Moody's (MCO) Investment Narrative?
items.summary: Moody's Corporation recently introduced zero-copy data sharing and expanded Model Context Protocol connectors so customers can tap its connected intelligence directly inside AI agents, models, and analytics environments, including through Snowflake Marketplace, without moving or duplicating data. items.title: Moody's (MCO) Stock Looks Reasonably Priced On Current Profitability
items.summary: Moody's has delivered a 3 year return of 34.1%. The more important issue for anyone looking at the stock today is whether that kind of share price performance lines up with the returns the business earns on its capital. With fresh product news around data and AI capabilities, the question now is how far the current US$485.69 price already reflects the profitability of the capital Moody's deploys. items.title: Billionaire Chris Hohn’s TCI Has 30% of Its $49.6 Billion Stock Portfolio in GE Aerospace
items.summary: One of the market's most concentrated funds just parked nearly a third of its money in a single industrial name, and the stock has barely moved this year. What does that bet reveal, and what should an ordinary retirement saver copy?

items.title: S&P’s NVIDIA Warning is Backward Looking Governance Theater That Gives Everyone an Opportunity to Buy at $150
items.summary: NVIDIA lost its CEO, drew a credit warning, and watched its stock slide nearly a third in a month. So why does one investor keep buying more every week, and which three numbers convinced him the real story lies elsewhere?

items.title: Nvidia’s Reliance on Huang Could Now Hurt Its Credit Rating
items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned, returned within days, and refused to name a successor. Now a bond rater is asking whether one founder holds too much of Nvidia's fate, and a deadline, hearings, and a key price level will decide the answer.

items.title: Corporate Bonds vs. Dividend Stocks: Which Pays a Retiree More Reliably?
items.summary: Corporate bond yields just hit a 12-month high, yet that fat payout hides trade-offs in price risk, reinvestment, and taxes. For retirees weighing bonds against Procter & Gamble and Coca-Cola, the tax bill may decide the winner.

items.title: Warren Buffett and Greg Abel Collect Billions From These Untouchable Berkshire Hathaway Dividend Stocks
items.summary: Five Berkshire holdings never budged in the latest 13F, yet their yields range from a sliver to a hefty payout. Which ones actually deliver income for retirees, and which carry risks that could trim the checks?
